statement: In an alphabet of $n$ letters, some ordered pairs (syllables) are indecent. A word is any finite or infinite sequence with no indecent syllable. Find the minimum number of indecent syllables that prevents any infinite word from existing.

Circles $\Omega$ and $\Gamma$ meet at $A, B$. Their centers' line meets $\Omega$ at $P$ and $\Gamma$ at $Q$ (same side as line $AB$, $Q$ closer to $AB$). Circle $\delta$ lies on the same side, touches $AB$ at $D$ and $\Gamma$ at $T$. Line $PD$ meets $\delta$ and $\Omega$ again at $K$ and $L$. Prove $\angle QTK = \angle DTL$.

Positive integer $d$ is not a perfect square. Let $s(n)$ = number of 1s among the first $n$ binary digits of $\sqrt{d}$ (including before the decimal point). Prove there exists $A$ with $s(n) > \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\,n}{2} - 2$ for all $n \geq A$.

Ten distinct positive reals have their 45 pairwise sums computed; 5 of these sums are equal. If the 45 pairwise products are also computed, find the maximum $k$ such that $k$ of these products can be equal.

An $m \times n$ table is tiled with $3 \times 1$ strips and $6 \mid mn$. Prove there exists a tiling of the same table with $2 \times 1$ dominoes such that each strip contains exactly one whole domino.

$G$ = centroid of $\triangle ABC$. Find the largest $\alpha$ such that some triangle has at least three of the six angles $\angle GAB, \angle GAC, \angle GBA, \angle GBC, \angle GCA, \angle GCB$ each $\geq \alpha$.
